audit_status.source_base: Greek 2 Corinthians text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for not receiving grace in vain, servant hardships, paradoxes, open heart, unequal yoke, temple of living Divine.

verses.restored: And working together, we also appeal that you not receive the grace of the Divine into emptiness.

familiar.text: We then, as workers together with him, beseech you also that ye receive not the grace of God in vain.

modern.text: As God’s fellow workers, then, we urge you not to receive God’s grace in vain.

original.text: Συνεργοῦντες δὲ καὶ παρακαλοῦμεν μὴ εἰς κενὸν τὴν χάριν τοῦ θεοῦ δέξασθαι ὑμᾶς·

verses.restored: For he says, In an acceptable season I listened to you, and in a day of salvation/healing I helped you. Look, now is the well-accepted season; look, now is the day of salvation/healing.

familiar.text: (For he saith, I have heard thee in a time accepted, and in the day of salvation have I succoured thee: behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation.)

modern.text: For He says: “In the time of favor I heard you, and in the day of salvation I helped you.” Behold, now is the time of favor; now is the day of salvation!

original.text: λέγει γάρ· Καιρῷ δεκτῷ ἐπήκουσά σου καὶ ἐν ἡμέρᾳ σωτηρίας ἐβοήθησά σοι· ἰδοὺ νῦν καιρὸς εὐπρόσδεκτος, ἰδοὺ νῦν ἡμέρα σωτηρίας·

verses.restored: Giving no stumbling in anything, so that the service/ministry may not be faulted,

familiar.text: Giving no offence in any thing, that the ministry be not blamed:

modern.text: We put no obstacle in anyone’s way, so that no one can discredit our ministry.

original.text: μηδεμίαν ἐν μηδενὶ διδόντες προσκοπήν, ἵνα μὴ μωμηθῇ ἡ διακονία,

verses.restored: but in everything commending ourselves as servants of the Divine: in much endurance, in pressures, in necessities, in constraints,

familiar.text: But in all things approving ourselves as the ministers of God, in much patience, in afflictions, in necessities, in distresses,

modern.text: Rather, as servants of God we commend ourselves in every way: in great endurance; in troubles, hardships, and calamities;

original.text: ἀλλʼ ἐν παντὶ ⸀συνιστάνοντες ἑαυτοὺς ὡς θεοῦ διάκονοι· ἐν ὑπομονῇ πολλῇ, ἐν θλίψεσιν, ἐν ἀνάγκαις, ἐν στενοχωρίαις,

verses.restored: in beatings, in prisons, in riots, in labors, in sleepless nights, in fastings,

familiar.text: In stripes, in imprisonments, in tumults, in labours, in watchings, in fastings;

modern.text: in beatings, imprisonments, and riots; in labor, sleepless nights, and hunger;

original.text: ἐν πληγαῖς, ἐν φυλακαῖς, ἐν ἀκαταστασίαις, ἐν κόποις, ἐν ἀγρυπνίαις, ἐν νηστείαις,

verses.restored: in purity, in knowledge, in patience, in kindness, in holy Spirit, in unhypocritical love,

familiar.text: By pureness, by knowledge, by longsuffering, by kindness, by the Holy Ghost, by love unfeigned,

modern.text: in purity, knowledge, patience, and kindness; in the Holy Spirit and in sincere love;

original.text: ἐν ἁγνότητι, ἐν γνώσει, ἐν μακροθυμίᾳ, ἐν χρηστότητι, ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ, ἐν ἀγάπῃ ἀνυποκρίτῳ,

verses.restored: in word of truth, in power of the Divine, through the weapons of righteousness/justice on the right and left,

familiar.text: By the word of truth, by the power of God, by the armour of righteousness on the right hand and on the left,

modern.text: in truthful speech and in the power of God; with the weapons of righteousness in the right hand and in the left;

original.text: ἐν λόγῳ ἀληθείας, ἐν δυνάμει θεοῦ· διὰ τῶν ὅπλων τῆς δικαιοσύνης τῶν δεξιῶν καὶ ἀριστερῶν,

verses.restored: through glory and dishonor, through harmful report and good report; as deceivers and true,

familiar.text: By honour and dishonour, by evil report and good report: as deceivers, and yet true;

modern.text: through glory and dishonor, slander and praise; viewed as imposters, yet genuine;

original.text: διὰ δόξης καὶ ἀτιμίας, διὰ δυσφημίας καὶ εὐφημίας· ὡς πλάνοι καὶ ἀληθεῖς,

verses.restored: as unknown and well known, as dying and look—we live; as disciplined and not killed,

familiar.text: As unknown, and yet well known; as dying, and, behold, we live; as chastened, and not killed;

modern.text: as unknown, yet well-known; dying, and yet we live on; punished, yet not killed;

original.text: ὡς ἀγνοούμενοι καὶ ἐπιγινωσκόμενοι, ὡς ἀποθνῄσκοντες καὶ ἰδοὺ ζῶμεν, ὡς παιδευόμενοι καὶ μὴ θανατούμενοι,

verses.restored: as grieving yet always rejoicing, as poor yet enriching many, as having nothing and possessing all things.

familiar.text: As sorrowful, yet alway rejoicing; as poor, yet making many rich; as having nothing, and yet possessing all things.

modern.text: sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; poor, yet making many rich; having nothing, and yet possessing everything.

original.text: ὡς λυπούμενοι ἀεὶ δὲ χαίροντες, ὡς πτωχοὶ πολλοὺς δὲ πλουτίζοντες, ὡς μηδὲν ἔχοντες καὶ πάντα κατέχοντες.

verses.restored: Our mouth has opened to you, Corinthians; our heart has been widened.

familiar.text: O ye Corinthians, our mouth is open unto you, our heart is enlarged.

modern.text: We have spoken freely to you, Corinthians. Our hearts are open wide.

original.text: Τὸ στόμα ἡμῶν ἀνέῳγεν πρὸς ὑμᾶς, Κορίνθιοι, ἡ καρδία ἡμῶν πεπλάτυνται·

verses.restored: You are not constrained in us, but you are constrained in your own inward parts.

familiar.text: Ye are not straitened in us, but ye are straitened in your own bowels.

modern.text: It is not our affection, but yours, that is restrained.

original.text: οὐ στενοχωρεῖσθε ἐν ἡμῖν, στενοχωρεῖσθε δὲ ἐν τοῖς σπλάγχνοις ὑμῶν·

verses.restored: In the same exchange, as to children I speak, be widened also.

familiar.text: Now for a recompence in the same, (I speak as unto my children,) be ye also enlarged.

modern.text: As a fair exchange, I ask you as my children: Open wide your hearts also. Do Not Be Unequally Yoked

original.text: τὴν δὲ αὐτὴν ἀντιμισθίαν, ὡς τέκνοις λέγω, πλατύνθητε καὶ ὑμεῖς.

verses.restored: Do not become unequally yoked with untrusting ones; for what partnership have righteousness/justice and lawlessness? Or what fellowship has light with darkness?

familiar.text: Be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers: for what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness? and what communion hath light with darkness?

modern.text: Do not be unequally yoked with unbelievers. For what partnership can righteousness have with wickedness? Or what fellowship does light have with darkness?

original.text: Μὴ γίνεσθε ἑτεροζυγοῦντες ἀπίστοις· τίς γὰρ μετοχὴ δικαιοσύνῃ καὶ ἀνομίᾳ, ⸂ἢ τίς⸃ κοινωνία φωτὶ πρὸς σκότος;

verses.restored: What harmony has Messiah with Belial? Or what share has a trusting one with an untrusting one?

familiar.text: And what concord hath Christ with Belial? or what part hath he that believeth with an infidel?

modern.text: What harmony is there between Christ and Belial? Or what does a believer have in common with an unbeliever?

original.text: τίς δὲ συμφώνησις ⸀Χριστοῦ πρὸς Βελιάρ, ἢ τίς μερὶς πιστῷ μετὰ ἀπίστου;

verses.restored: What agreement has a temple of the Divine with idols? For we are temple of living Divine, just as the Divine said: I will dwell in them and walk among them, and I will be their Divine, and they will be my people.

familiar.text: And what agreement hath the temple of God with idols? for ye are the temple of the living God; as God hath said, I will dwell in them, and walk in them; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.

modern.text: What agreement can exist between the temple of God and idols? For we are the temple of the living God. As God has said: “I will dwell with them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they will be My people.”

original.text: τίς δὲ συγκατάθεσις ναῷ θεοῦ μετὰ εἰδώλων; ⸂ἡμεῖς γὰρ ναὸς θεοῦ ἐσμεν⸃ ζῶντος· καθὼς εἶπεν ὁ θεὸς ὅτι Ἐνοικήσω ἐν αὐτοῖς καὶ ἐμπεριπατήσω, καὶ ἔσομαι αὐτῶν θεός, καὶ αὐτοὶ ἔσονταί ⸀μου λαός.

verses.restored: Therefore come out from their midst and be separated, says the Lord, and touch nothing unclean; and I will receive you,

familiar.text: Wherefore come out from among them, and be ye separate, saith the Lord, and touch not the unclean thing; and I will receive you,

modern.text: “Therefore come out from among them and be separate, says the Lord. Touch no unclean thing, and I will receive you.”

original.text: διὸ ἐξέλθατε ἐκ μέσου αὐτῶν, καὶ ἀφορίσθητε, λέγει κύριος, καὶ ἀκαθάρτου μὴ ἅπτεσθε· κἀγὼ εἰσδέξομαι ὑμᾶς·

verses.restored: and I will be Father to you, and you will be sons and daughters to me, says Lord Almighty.

familiar.text: And will be a Father unto you, and ye shall be my sons and daughters, saith the Lord Almighty.

modern.text: And: “I will be a Father to you, and you will be My sons and daughters, says the Lord Almighty.”

original.text: καὶ ἔσομαι ὑμῖν εἰς πατέρα, καὶ ὑμεῖς ἔσεσθέ μοι εἰς υἱοὺς καὶ θυγατέρας, λέγει κύριος παντοκράτωρ.

translation_notes: The unequal-yoke section should be handled as covenant/participation discernment, not contempt for outsiders. It follows the open-heart appeal and must not negate Paul's reconciliation ministry.
The hardship catalog presents weakness and pressure as signs of servant integrity, not failure.
